questions.q: What is work, and why is it said that all work has dignity?
answer: Work is any activity done to produce goods or services, meet needs, or earn a living. It turns human effort and skill into the things and services that people require.

answer.text: A farmer grows food, a teacher educates, a cleaner keeps places healthy, a carpenter builds — each is necessary, and society could not function without any of them.
Because every kind of work contributes to the common good, no work is 'high' or 'low'; all of it deserves respect. This idea is called the dignity of labour.
We depend on one another's work, so respecting every worker is both fair and necessary for society to run.

questions.q: Distinguish between paid and unpaid work, with examples.
answer: Work can be classified by whether it is directly paid for.

answer.text: Work done in return for wages or income — for example, a shopkeeper selling goods, a driver, or a factory worker. It brings a direct earning.
Work done without direct payment but which is still very valuable — for example, household work, caring for children and the elderly, or farming to feed one's own family.
Unpaid work, often done at home and frequently by women, is essential to society even though it earns no wage and is easily overlooked. Recognising its value is important for fairness.
